report:
Assessed the complete signature.storage claim, all nine ordinary implementation entries, and the one associated TODO test. Requirements: source CST remains input in its own stash; checked types, binders, predicates and retained alias applications live in a separate result stash; no result contains tree-sitter references or pointers into the CST stash. Captured checking design and the linked Stash architectural rationale, which specifies structural copying between owners and debug stash identity checks rather than database-global meaning for numeric handles.

Implementation: Check::new holds an immutable source_stash and creates a fresh target_stash. Check::finish in sig.rs moves that target into Stashed::new with the checked root. CheckGenerics allocates the parameter slice in target; semantic parameter identities are copied handles, not CST pointers. PathSegment::check_type_args checks source syntax and allocates both types and argument slices in target. TypeCst::check recursively translates references, tuples, slices, arrays and function types using target allocation. Resolved named aliases retain definition identity with already-checked target arguments. Existing semantic Self resolutions come from the current checking context rather than raw source types. lower_predicates in trait_env.rs builds checked subject types, trait arguments and predicate slices in target, and Check::complete_parameter_env combines target-owned predicate values.

open_owner in fns.rs calls signature.copy_into(target_stash) before using the owner binder's types, predicate slices and generic slice. It then constructs new Self/predicate values and final function signature collections in the same target. Captured Binder::stash_copy explicitly copies both value and generic slice. The initial sage-stash implementation defines Stashed as owning its Stash and root; copy_into invokes structural StashCopy. Ptr and Slice implementations read source entries, recursively copy values and allocate destination entries. Captured derive implementation generates that recursive copy for every struct field and enum payload, covering derived Ty and alias representations rather than relying on a shallow Copy of their stash handles. Captured Ty/Alias/Binder definitions contain semantic handles, scalar values and destination-relative Ptr/Slice fields, not parser-node borrows.

apply_external_adt_signature in external_syms.rs accepts explicit type arguments already in target, folds source-owned defaults into target with earlier substitutions, and folds the declaration predicate environment into target. Substitute entries contain target-owned Ty values, so returning a substituted Ty directly is correct for this path. ty_fold.rs default_fold_ty and alias helpers reallocate nested ADT arguments, named/opaque alias arguments, associated projection Self/trait arguments, reference/array/slice inners, tuples and function types. Parameter and identity-only leaves remain scalar handles. fold_parameter_env rebuilds each predicate and its argument slices. The external metadata signature lowerers allocate their original semantic products in their own fresh stash; external application then crosses the ownership boundary explicitly. Stashed::new retains ownership and computes the rooted fingerprint; fingerprinting is not treated as proof that every pointer is valid.

The sole associated test todo::checking_signature_storage is explicitly deferred and contains no assertions. It specifies representative structural signature traversals after parser/source-stash borrows have ended, retained aliases and predicates, and detection of cross-stash pointers. That is an honest remaining verification requirement: completing it requires source-derived nested signatures, scopes that end source borrows before result traversal, and assertions that exercise the entire reachable result graph (with debug stash identity validation where applicable). Coverage should distinguish target-owned substitutions from source-owned default/predicate inputs and include the alias variants supported by their producers. The placeholder is not claimed to establish these guarantees, and no test execution is inferred from its annotation. No new suspected defect was identified in the inspected allocation/copy routes.

Commands executed: fresh review start with coordinator instructions, source and complete-test inspection, review read captures for design/RFD, Ty/Alias/Binder representations and the structural-copy derive. No tests or build were executed by this reviewer; central suite results remain separate. No source edits. No requested edits, with the existing test TODO explicitly retained rather than full verification claimed.
